title: Scrum Backlog Management
description: Comprehensive framework for structuring, prioritizing, refining, and maintaining a high-value Scrum product backlog.

categories.name: Backlog Structuring & Item Hierarchy
aspects: Epics, Features, and User Stories decomposition hierarchy
Applying the INVEST criteria to create independent and testable stories
Formulating unambiguous Acceptance Criteria using Given/When/Then (Gherkin)
Vertical user story slicing techniques (workflow, business rule, and data variations)
Spike stories: timeboxed research, prototyping, and de-risking unknowns

categories.name: Prioritization & Value Ordering
aspects: Weighted Shortest Job First (WSJF) and Cost of Delay calculations
MoSCoW method (Must Have, Should Have, Could Have, Won't Have) calibration
Kano model analysis (differentiating delighters from basic expectations)
Value vs Effort / Complexity 2x2 matrix ranking
Handling stakeholder urgency vs verified customer and business ROI

categories.name: Backlog Refinement & Estimation
aspects: Establishing an effective refinement cadence (e.g. 5-10% of sprint capacity)
Relative sizing (Story Points, T-shirt sizing) vs No-Estimates throughput forecasting
Asynchronous and distributed Planning Poker practices
Definition of Ready (DoR): balance between clarity and over-specification
Pre-Sprint Planning story readiness review and dependency unblocking

categories.name: Technical Debt, Bugs & Quality Items
aspects: Capacity allocation policies for tech debt and refactoring (e.g. 15-20% budget)
Defect triage workflows: classifying critical hotfixes vs backlog bugs
Documenting Non-Functional Requirements (NFRs: security, scale, performance)
Feature deprecation and tech sunset backlog items
Architectural Runway items for enabling future feature delivery

categories.name: Stakeholder & Roadmap Alignment
aspects: Connecting strategic Product Roadmap themes to individual backlog epics
Managing unscheduled 'drive-by' stakeholder requests without sprint disruption
Closing the loop: feeding customer interviews and product analytics into backlog
Backlog transparency and visibility radiators (Jira, Linear, physical boards)
Release planning: milestone forecasting and minimum viable release scope

categories.name: Backlog Hygiene & Pruning
aspects: Tackling backlog bloat: automated aging thresholds and archival policies
Pruning stale ideas: respectfully closing items older than 3 to 6 months
Maintaining optimal backlog depth (typically 2 to 3 sprints of refined work)
Aligning Acceptance Criteria with the Definition of Done (DoD)
Translating Sprint Retrospective improvement experiments into backlog items

categories.name: Flow, Metrics & Forecasting
aspects: Cycle Time and Lead Time tracking from 'Idea' to 'Production'
Cumulative Flow Diagrams (CFD) to identify bottlenecks in refinement stages
Monte Carlo simulation models for probabilistic delivery forecasting
Work-in-Progress (WIP) limits for items in backlog refinement
Value Stream Mapping to eliminate handoff delays in backlog readiness
